case_data.title: Leverhulme Trust Funded StudentXGenAI Project (Student Experiences of GenAI Project )
case_data.provide-a-brief-description-of-the-proje:
This project consisted of a survey of over 7000 UK university students, interviews with 20 students and a GenAI assisted scoping review. This research project adopted a mixed-methods approach, integrating both qualitative and quantitative research methods, to comprehensively explore students' experiences and attitudes towards the use of AI tools in UK higher education. 

It had 4 key aims. 1.) To examine UK university students' perceived usefulness and acceptance of AI tools for learning. 2.) To investigate the diverse uses of AI tools in academic tasks, their frequency, and the underlying reasons for these usage patterns among UK university students. 3.) To explore both the challenges and facilitators affecting the adoption and wider utilisation of AI tools in UK universities, including both user-level and system-level factors. 4). To co-develop evidence-based recommendations for enhancing AI tools use and implementation in the education sector, in collaboration with relevant communities such as students, educators, university administrators, and AI developers.
case_data.what-limitations-to-the-project-should-b: The survey sample was limited to volunteers, so those with strong views may have been more likely to be iinvolved. We did advertise the survey for users and non-users of GenAi.
case_data.headline-findings:
1. Students were asked if they used GenAI when they weren't allowed - the message is clear - the majority of students are honest the majority of the time.
2. There is a discourse in the media that all students are using GenAI - this is not the case with our data - 70% were users and 30% with non users.
3. The main motivations for using GenAI are efficiency,
4. The drive for efficiency is balanced by the desire for students to act ethically - students want to do the work themselves, they worry about the ethical and enivronmental impact of GenAI.
5. Students are using GenAI for a number of tasks related to the learning and assessment process but are stopping short, in most cases, of directly editing their assessments. The problem is, we are unsure what impact the cognitive offloading of reading, brainstorming and structuring of assessments has on students.
case_data.inclusion-efforts: The survey was administered to students via an accessible online platform (MS Forms).

project-goals: Methods: Create re-usable participation tools & methods
Quantitative: Generate statistical evidence on public attitudes to AI
Qualitative: Capture qualitative evidence on public attitudes to AI
Empowerment: Build community power with respect to AI
where-were-participants-from: UK universities in England, Scotland and Northern Ireland
